messages:
alex: Heads-up — we've been iterating on per-org enforcement and I want to propose a pattern: token-bucket for TPM/RPM + an independent concurrency cap. Short thread on tradeoffs?

pj: +1. want the concrete numbers though. are we keeping burst credits or moving to strictly smoothed window? :thinking:

alex: prefer keeping a small burst credit pool that decays over time (credits TTL) so short spikes don't break customers. but primary defence should be steady RPM/TPM.

sophie: can you sketch how concurrency interacts? e.g., 200 TPM but 10 concurrent inflight — what happens at sustained spikes?

alex: good Q. model: allow burst credits to pay for extra tokens when TPM exceeded. concurrency cap is orthogonal — it prevents head-of-line resource exhaustion. if concurrency hit, new requests get 429 with Retry-After or are queued depending on route.

kevin: implementation note: our API gateway currently enforces per-key rpm via lua module. duplicating enforcement in runtime is painful. do we need dual enforcement?

pj: dual enforcement gives fast fail at edge and final safety in runtime. migrate to edge-fast-fail + runtime-metering for accounting and fallback.

lisa: telemetry requirement: dashboard must show realtime "burst balance" for orgs, concurrency headroom, and 1m/5m/1h TPM curves. ops needs headroom alerts.

alex: agreed. also add a "grace mode" rule: if org was recently under SLA and hits limit, allow a short soft-fail window (exponential backoff) before hard-blocking. helps SDKs that retry aggressively.

pj: can we express policy in config like:
```
policy: {
  rpm: 1200,
  tpm: 30000,
  burst_credits: 1000,
  credit_ttl_s: 300,
  concurrency_limit: 20,
  soft_grace: {window_s: 60, factor: 0.5}
}
```

kevin: looks fine. question: how do we charge tokens for streaming responses? tokens are trickier — streaming can accumulate many tokens while concurrency holds a slot.

alex: we bill/consume tokens progressively. burst credits should pay for initial tokens; runtime enforces token consumption per chunk and can free concurrency slot if client aborts. we must avoid long-lived streams blocking concurrency quota. maybe cap stream lifetime or have separate streaming concurrency.

sophie: UX: console should show per-route concurrency and allow an org-admin to request temporary burst increases (manual approval flow). For sales, we need a one-click override that creates a temporary higher burst pool + audit trail.

pj: how about automatic temporary boost for orgs on paid plans if they have unused reserved capacity? tie to Dedicated capacity pools.

lisa: alerting: two alerts — approaching concurrency cap (>=80%) and burst depleted (<=10%). both go to oncall and account owner. also add an "impact forecast" for next 5m based on recent rate to avoid surprises.

kevin: deployment plan: start with runtime-only enforcement in alpha test orgs, then enable edge-fast-fail in a shadow mode for 24h (no blocking, just logs + metrics), then flip to enforcement with canary 10% traffic. deploy-bot will kick off canary.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: route-rate-limiter v3 -> canary(10%) -> targets: west-1 gateway nodes. ETA 12:00 UTC.

alex: compatibility note: SDKs need to surface new 429 with body that includes {reason, retry_after_s, burst_balance}. Add docs.

pj: also add admin API to drain concurrency for debugging (admin/drain?reason=...), with RBAC.

kevin: one more: we must be careful with cross-org proxies (shared IP). enforcement should be per-org id, not per-IP. gateway must extract org-id early and attach to token.

lisa: can we store burst credits in Redis, TTL set to credit_ttl_s? need to check scale. prefer sharded counters with CAS.

alex: yep. design doc milestone: I'll write a short proposal and include these config examples + migration steps. target RFC by EOD Friday. anyone want to be co-reviewer?

sophie: i'll co-review.

pj: count me in for implementation review and metrics spec.

ratebot: NOTE: simulated load test tomorrow 09:00 UTC (perflab). will seed 50 orgs with burst patterns.

kevin: cool. I'll schedule gateway shadow run after load test.

alex: thanks all. short follow-up: add a field on console "burst history" graph (1h/24h) and exportable CSV for billing disputes.

lisa: added to TODOs. :thumbsup:
